notes:
- **Archie now comes with the AI included, if you want it that way.** $59 a month or $599 a year
  buys the same plan plus $25 of Claude usage every month, so there is no AI account to open and
  no second bill. Tick "With the AI included" when you pick a plan. Your agent runs on our
  Anthropic account, which means what you write to it, and the mail it reads and writes for you,
  passes through our server on the way to Anthropic; nothing there writes it down, we keep no
  copy, and we use none of it. When the $25 is used, your agent pauses until next month. Connect
  an AI account of your own at any point and it carries on from there, with nothing to switch.
- On that plan, and on the free credits, the Response quality control on an agent's page now says
  that it changes nothing until you connect an AI account of your own, instead of looking like a
  setting that does something.
- **Any service that publishes an MCP server can be connected now.** GitHub, Linear, Stripe and
  Cloudflare are on the Connections tab under MCP servers, and "Another MCP server" takes any
  address you have. Paste the key, Archie asks the server what it can do, and your agent can use
  every tool the server offers: the read-only ones on the spot, and anything that changes
  something only after you approve it, the same way a web request works today.
- **Ten more services have an add-on that knows how to use them:** Airtable, Calendly, GitLab,
  Lunch Money, Mercury, Readwise, Stripe, Splitwise, YNAB and Zotero. Each one was written from
  that service's own documentation, so your agent is told the real endpoints instead of guessing.
- A key you paste for a service no add-on uses works anyway. Before, "what is on my Calendly"
  was answered with "Calendly is not connected" while the key sat right there.
- A connection assigned to somebody by name on a shared agent is now visible to them. Karla
  asked whether Calendly was connected and was told no; it was, and it was hers.
- **A routine that missed its time because the laptop was shut says so.** The Routines card
  names the sleep and opens a list of steps for keeping this computer awake, instead of sending
  you to look at Archie, where nothing is wrong.
- A morning routine that missed 8:00 am now runs any time before noon, an afternoon one runs
  until 6:00 pm, and an evening one runs until midnight and never after. The old rule gave up two
  hours after the time, which on a laptop opened at 10:00 am meant last night's routines never
  ran and this morning's barely did.
- The Routines tab checks how each routine is doing every few seconds. It used to look once when
  the page opened, so a routine that had recovered could stay marked red all day.
- **Remind me to pay Sam back on Friday** sets a reminder for Friday at 9:00 am and says so, with
  Noon and 6:00 pm one tap away, instead of stopping to ask for a time. "Pay my electric bill on
  the 5th" sets it for the next 5th and asks whether you want it every month; a Yes turns it into
  a routine, and a repeating reminder is a routine now, with no skill needed.
- **Tell your agent what you wish it could do** and it asks one question at a time, as buttons,
  about your life and never about the machinery. The card says what it assumed. It refuses to
  invent a time, a time zone or a name you did not give it.
- "Every Friday morning, tell me what bills are due" sets up a routine over a skill you already
  have, offering a store routine first when one fits. Run it now is one tap after Keep it.
- A store routine runs the skills it came with, so its edit form says what it runs instead of
  offering tickboxes. Only a routine you built shows the checklist.
- When your agent has a document in its knowledge base, it reads it and answers, instead of
  telling somebody on Slack to open a file they cannot see.
- On the edition that answers one person, the two buttons for adding a second are gone. Both
  could only produce an error.
- Fixed: a network failure said "network request failed" and nothing else. It now says why: the
  name did not resolve, the connection timed out, or the secure handshake failed, which are three
  different things to go and fix.
- Fixed: a document over the size limit was cut twice, losing the end of it a second time.
- Fixed: the crash reporter could turn a recoverable crash into Archie quitting outright when the
  terminal it was writing to had gone away.
